chapter: Reel 2: Los Angeles musicians, the Apex and Cotton Club
title: Teddy Buckner and the Louis Armstrong influence
summary: Howard calls Buckner a fine musician who patterned himself on Armstrong, which helped and hurt him; he cannot say when Buckner came.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, what about Teddy now, Teddy Buckner?
Teddy? Fine musician. Didn't have nothing to say about anybody. Put that horn up there and play, and we'd play.
Now, there was a period when a lot of trumpeters wanted to be like Louis Armstrong, and it seems like he would seem to pattern his style after Louis.
He did.
Did that help him or hurt him at that period?
Well, it did both.
Sometimes, when you're trying to be
Well, it did both.
Well, (inaudible).
My wife.
But he still has a good band, actually.
And I guess you've known him ever since the time he came to Los Angeles.
Who?
Teddy Buckner /
Oh, yeah.
Do you know about when that was, when he came here?
I haven't the slightest idea when he came.
Do you know any of the bands he worked with around?
No.
Did he work with Les Hite or anybody like that, do you remember?
I can't remember.
